Here are some useful resources for using R.

## Useful cheatsheets

- [For base R (general)](https://www.rstudio.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/10/r-cheat-sheet-3.pdf)
- [Other cheatsheets](https://www.rstudio.com/resources/cheatsheets/)


## Extra R tutorials

- [Very basic](http://www.r-tutor.com/r-introduction) 
- [General R introduction up to complex statistics all here](https://ourcodingclub.github.io/tutorials.html)
- [A bit more complex/broad](https://datacarpentry.org/R-ecology-lesson/01-intro-to-r.html)

For those looking to go beyond this course [TidyVerse](https://www.tidyverse.org/learn/) or [Advanced R](http://adv-r.had.co.nz/)


## R and RStudio

If you want to use R Studio (which we reconmend), you will need to download and install both R and R Studio

- [R](https://cran.r-project.org/)
- [R-studio](https://www.rstudio.com/products/rstudio/#Desktop): select the Desktop version and make sure it is the free version!

## Tutorial on R and stats (plus its very pretty)

[A tutorial on some basics of R, there are also statistics modules here too](https://tinystats.github.io/teacups-giraffes-and-statistics/01_introToR.html)


## A guide to dbinom

[A guide to dbinom](https://www.statology.org/a-guide-to-dbinom-pbinom-qbinom-and-rbinom-in-r/)

(this might help with other function, like dnorm() etc. for the normal distribution)


## Resources for Linear Models

[Table showing how some common statistical tests are actually linear models](https://lindeloev.github.io/tests-as-linear/linear_tests_cheat_sheet.pdf)


[Regression web page](https://bioceed.uib.no/dropfolder/sites/bioSTATS-and-R/StatisticsInR/2.1_simple_linear_regression.html)
